newsitem.title: USA: Bank stocks rally amid benign economic data.
newsitem.headline: Bank stocks rally amid benign economic data.

text.p: Benign economic data, released Tuesday morning, eased inflation fears and added momentum to the rally in banking and financial services stocks, analysts said.
Building on solid gains seen on Monday, shares of the major U.S. banks jumped Tuesday and were among the most heavily traded issues at midday.
Chase Manhattan Corp gained 2-7/8 to 90-3/8, Citicorp increased 4-1/8 to 111-3/8, NationsBank Corp added 2-1/8 to 59-7/8, and Bank of New York jumped 1-7/8 to 39.
The Philadelphia Stock Exchange banking index soared almost 20 points or 3.48 percent to 585.53.

Banking stocks started to rise Monday in advance of the first quarter Employment Cost Index from the U.S. Labor Department, released Tuesday. The gains continued Tuesday after investors perceived the softer-than-forecast data as a sign that inflation was not a problem and that the Federal Reserve may refrain from raising interest rates.
But the favorable economic data only added to the positive buzz surrounding banking and financial services stocks, analysts said.
Gains in banking stocks have also been driven by strong first quarter earnings, strength in the bond market and an overdue rebound in the sector.

"It's partly due to the bond market rally and partly due to the fact that they've been corrected more than the market overall. They were getting down to (price/earnings) multiples that many perceived as too low," said First International Asset Management's Michael Schroeder.
Prior to its recent slip, the bank index had outpaced the broader market, jumping 20.7 percent at its March 10 peak, compared to a 9.9 rise in the S&P 500 at that point.

A correction slammed both indices, and banking stocks dropped below the Standard & Poor's 500. Bank stocks have now resumed the lead, up 8.9 percent for the year, compared with a 6.1 percent rise in the S&P 500.

"The most favorable news for the banking stocks has been the strength of earnings. The major banks have either met or exceeded expectations and that certainly bodes well for the sector as a whole," said Raphael Soifer, a bank analyst with Brown Brothers Harriman.
Banking stocks "really got hit hard in that downturn. What drove the downturn wasn't earnings, it was just interst rate fears," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist with Kemper Funds.
Some analysts suggested banking stocks will be volatile in the short-term due to lingering fears over interest rates.

Analysts said investors will continue to take signals from a slew of economic data expected later this week, such as the first quarter gross domestic product report, the April National Association of Purchasing Management index, and the index of leading economic indicators.
But even if the Federal Reserve did decide to raise interest rates marginally, prospects for banking stocks would not deteriorate, some analysts said.

"Even if there's a rise in rates, the worst it would be all year in aggreagate would be 75 basis point, and that's not going to turn banks from being a great investment to being a horrible one," Froehlich said.
The Fed's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee next meets May 20.
Wells Fargo and Co gained 8-7/8 to 268-5/8, Mellon Bank Corp increased 1-1/4 to 80-3/4 and Bankers Trust New York Corp firmed 1-1/2 to 81-1/4.

Financial company stocks have followed the same pattern as banking stocks. Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc increased 1 to 34, Merrill Lynch and Co Inc added 1-1/4 to 80-3/4, and Alex. Brown Inc gained 1-3/8 to 64-5/8.
